# Radiofrequency Ablation Clinical Compass

## CPT Codes

| CPT | Description | RVU | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 64633 | Destruction by neurolytic agent, paravertebral facet joint nerve; cervical or thoracic, single facet joint | 5.12 | Cervical/thoracic RFA — single level |
| 64634 | Destruction by neurolytic agent, paravertebral facet joint nerve; cervical or thoracic, each additional facet joint | 2.44 | Add-on code — each additional cervical/thoracic level |
| 64635 | Destruction by neurolytic agent, paravertebral facet joint nerve; lumbar or sacral, single facet joint | 4.88 | Lumbar/sacral RFA — single level |
| 64636 | Destruction by neurolytic agent, paravertebral facet joint nerve; lumbar or sacral, each additional facet joint | 2.28 | Add-on code — each additional lumbar/sacral level |

## ICD-10 Codes

| ICD-10 | Description | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| M54.5 | Low back pain | Primary code for lumbar facet syndrome |
| M47.816 | Spondylosis without myelopathy or radiculopathy, lumbar region | Lumbar facet arthropathy |
| M47.812 | Spondylosis without myelopathy or radiculopathy, cervical region | Cervical facet arthropathy |
| M54.2 | Cervicalgia | Cervical facet pain |
| M54.59 | Other low back pain | Non-specific low back pain |

## Payer Requirements

Tabs: Medicare | Medicaid | Private Insurance

### Medicare

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- Two positive diagnostic medial branch blocks (MBBs) with ≥80% pain relief each
- MBBs performed on separate dates (typically 2–4 weeks apart)
- Pain diary documenting % relief at 30 min and 2 hours post-MBB
- Clinical diagnosis of facetogenic pain (axial pain, extension-provoked)
- Documentation of conservative therapy failure: ≥3 months PT and analgesics
- Imaging (X-ray or MRI) showing facet arthropathy
- Frequency limit: typically once per 6 months per region (Medicare LCD)

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Two positive diagnostic MBBs with ≥80% relief each
- ✓ Axial spine pain with facetogenic pattern
- ✓ Failed conservative therapy for ≥3 months
- ✓ No predominant radicular component

**Reimbursement:** Medicare covers RFA under applicable LCD. Two positive confirmatory MBBs are required. Fluoroscopic guidance is included in the CPT code. Document MBB dates, % relief, and duration of relief.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicare (CMS) | Covered per LCD; requires 2 positive MBBs (≥80% relief each); once per 6 months per region | Yes |

### Medicaid

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- State-specific prior authorization required
- Two positive diagnostic MBBs documentation
- Clinical diagnosis documentation
- Conservative therapy failure documentation

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Two positive diagnostic MBBs with ≥80% relief
- ✓ Axial pain with facetogenic pattern
- ✓ Failed conservative therapy

**Reimbursement:** Medicaid coverage varies by state. Prior authorization typically required. Some states require 3 positive MBBs or have stricter criteria.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Medicaid (state-specific) | Prior auth required; MBB requirements vary by state | Yes |

### Private Insurance

**Prior Authorization Requirements**
- Prior authorization required by most commercial payers
- Two positive diagnostic MBBs with ≥50–80% pain relief (threshold varies by payer)
- MBBs performed on separate dates
- Pain diary documenting % relief post-MBB
- Clinical documentation of facetogenic pain pattern
- Imaging showing facet arthropathy
- Documentation of ≥3 months conservative therapy failure

**Medical Necessity Criteria**
- ✓ Two positive diagnostic MBBs (threshold varies: ≥50–80% by payer)
- ✓ Axial spine pain with facetogenic pattern
- ✓ Failed conservative therapy (PT, NSAIDs) for ≥3 months

**Reimbursement:** Commercial payers typically cover RFA with prior authorization and positive MBB documentation. Relief threshold varies (50–80%). Some payers require only one positive MBB.

**Known Payer Policies**

| Payer | Policy | Covered |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Aetna | Covered; requires 2 positive MBBs with ≥80% relief each | Yes |
| UnitedHealthcare | Covered with prior auth; 2 positive MBBs required | Yes |
| BCBS (most plans) | Covered; 2 positive MBBs with ≥50% relief; prior auth required | Yes |
| Cigna | Covered with prior auth; positive MBB documentation required | Yes |
| Humana | Covered; prior auth and 2 positive MBBs required | Yes |

## Required Documentation

### Diagnostic MBB Documentation
- □ MBB procedure notes for both blocks (dates, levels, agent, volume)
- □ Pain diary showing ≥80% relief at 30 min and 2 hours post-MBB for each block
- □ Duration of relief documentation (days/weeks)
- □ Functional improvement documentation post-MBB

### Imaging
- □ X-ray or MRI showing facet arthropathy or spondylosis at treated levels
- □ Absence of significant disc herniation or nerve root compression

### Clinical Documentation
- □ H&P documenting axial pain pattern, extension provocation, and referred pain distribution
- □ Pain scores at multiple visits (NRS or VAS)
- □ Functional impairment documentation
- □ Documentation of absence of predominant neurologic deficit

### Conservative Therapy
- □ PT notes documenting ≥3 months of spinal stabilization program
- □ NSAIDs or analgesics trial documentation

## Submission Process

1. Perform first diagnostic MBB with fluoroscopy — document % relief at 30 min and 2 hours
2. Perform second confirmatory MBB on a separate date (2–4 weeks later) — document % relief
3. Ensure both MBBs show ≥80% relief (or payer-specific threshold) at 30 min and 2 hours
4. Submit prior authorization with CPT codes (64635 ± 64636 for lumbar), ICD-10 codes, and MBB documentation
5. Include both MBB procedure notes, pain diaries, imaging report, and PT notes
6. Document levels treated and number of add-on codes needed
7. If denied for insufficient MBB relief, request peer-to-peer review
8. For repeat RFA: document duration of prior relief and recurrence of symptoms

## Common Denial Reasons

- ⚠ Insufficient MBB documentation — most common denial; document % relief at 30 min AND 2 hours for BOTH blocks
- ⚠ Only one positive MBB documented (most payers require two)
- ⚠ MBBs not performed on separate dates
- ⚠ Pain relief threshold not met (document ≥80% relief explicitly — not just 'significant improvement')
- ⚠ Missing pain diary documentation for post-MBB relief
- ⚠ Wrong CPT code for level (cervical vs. lumbar) or add-on codes not used correctly
- ⚠ Frequency limit exceeded — document recurrence of symptoms and duration of prior relief
- ⚠ Prior authorization not obtained before procedure
